newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end sharply lower.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures closed sharply lower but off the lowest levels of the session reached on selling that emerged following the afternoon release of U.S. retail sales data.
"After the Redbook we had our last dip to the lows," said one S&P 500 stock index trader on the floor of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
The Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Retail Sales Index rose 0.8 percent in the second week of fiscal March versus February and was up 8.3 percent compared to the same month a year ago.

The strong sales data fueled worries that the Federal Reserve is likely to raise interest rates to stem U.S. economic growth, possibly as early as next week's meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee.

"Now people are thinking that whenever the Fed does something, it does it in threes," said Kurt Schultz, a stock index analyst on the floor of the Chicago Merantile Exchange. Some participants therefore are thinking there could be a series of three 25-basis-point rate hikes, he said.
Premium narrowed on the decline, at times setting off arbitrage sell programs.
The theoretical fair value premium of the June S&P contract over the spot index is about 8.00 points, and sell programs were triggered at premiums of 7.00 points or less, traders said.
Still, Schultz noted that the June contract failed to penetrate Monday's lows at 790.00 and that strong support was evident at a trendline near 788.00.
Nikkei 225 stock index futures stayed in fairly narrow ranges, dipping early in the session but firming late in the day.
Traders also noted that some of the pressure may have been related to the expiration of the March contract at the end of this week.

At settlement, June S&P 500s were off 9.40 points at 795.00, Nasdaq 100s eased 8.50 to 837.50, Russell 2000s fell 3.00 points to 357.00, Value Line futures were off 9.25 points at 712.00, Nikkei 225 index futures gained 485.0 to 18,475.0 and Midcap 400s slipped 1.20 point to 263.80.
